subject: SIG crosswalk & evidence cadence — ClearLake Health RFI
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearlakehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlakehealth.com>, Bloomfield Security Consulting <sec-team@bloomfieldconsult.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearLake RFI: SIG questionnaire — control mapping and evidence cadence

Hi Lauren,

We're working through the SIG questionnaire for our upcoming procurement committee and have a couple of clarifications before we hand the packet to procurement. Two specific asks: 1) do you have a control crosswalk (SIG to SOC 2/ISO clauses) and a recommended evidence cadence (minimal artifacts vs full substantiation) we can include in the RFP response; 2) can you share examples of the types of artifacts you can provide on short notice (logs, key rotation proof, BOM for third-party infra)?

Timeline: the committee needs a consolidated packet by 2027-11-09. If we can get a draft crosswalk and a list of available artifacts this week, we can fold it into the RFP. Also please flag any questions that require legal or product review.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager
ClearLake Health
Attachment: sample_sig_request.docx (request template)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearlakehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearLake RFI: SIG questionnaire — control mapping and evidence cadence

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the note and timeline. We're happy to support the packet. Quick plan: 1) attached is a first-pass SIG-to-SOC2/ISO crosswalk tailored to common healthcare asks (CLH_SIG_crosswalk_v1.xlsx); 2) I've included a short evidence manifest (redwood_evidence_manifest.csv) that lists the artifact types we can produce on a 48–72 hour window vs. those that take longer (e.g., full interview transcripts, vendor attestation letters); 3) Karthik will follow up with the KMS/key rotation details you asked about.

Open items for your team: which control objectives are highest priority for the committee (data residency, encryption in transit/rest, privileged access)? If you can flag priorities I can reorder the crosswalk and annotate the ‘quick-deliver’ set.

Proposed cadence: we can deliver a marked-up crosswalk + quick artifacts by 2027-10-29, and a fuller substantiation bundle by 2027-11-04. If that works, let's lock a 30-minute walkthrough on 2027-11-05 to walk through the evidence and field any technical questions.

Attachments: CLH_SIG_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (control mapping), redwood_evidence_manifest.csv (artifact index)

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Assurance Operations — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearlakehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlakehealth.com>, Bloomfield Security Consulting <sec-team@bloomfieldconsult.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearLake RFI: SIG questionnaire — control mapping and evidence cadence

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups from Priya and Bloomfield after a quick review:

- Can you confirm the KMS model you use in Private deployments (customer-managed keys in KMS vs. Redwood-managed)? We need wording for the RFP about key custody and rotation proof.
- For privileged access, do you have playbooks or session recordings that we can reference as evidence? If so, what is the redaction process?
- We saw a note about ‘third-party infra BOM’ — would a tagged inventory (csv) + signed SLA excerpt be available as a one-off?

We uploaded a short artifact template to your Drive link to capture the items we expect for quick delivery. Our committee would prioritize encryption at rest, KMS custody, and privileged access controls. If you can indicate which artifacts you'll provide by 10/29 vs. the 11/04 full packet that will be most helpful.

Link: https://drive.clearlakehealth.com/sigs/CLH-RFP-2027-upload (we placed an intake stub)

Alex
Attachment: intake_index_template.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@clearlakehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearlakehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearLake RFI: SIG questionnaire — control mapping and evidence cadence

Hi Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the priority list. Short answers and plan below: 

1) KMS custody and rotation: For Redwood Private we offer both customer-managed keys (BYOK via customer KMS) and Redwood-hosted keys (we use AWS KMS with internal key rotation). For RFP language we typically provide a short clause and attach a rotation summary PDF. See attachment: kms-key-rotation-summary.pdf (includes rotation cadence, KMS key IDs redacted to tenant prefix). We can provide signed attestation for BYOK setups on request (legal review required for attestation wording).

2) Privileged access evidence: We can provide exported session audit logs (timestamped), the privilege escalation playbook excerpt (redacted), and a recorded red-team runbook demo snapshot. Session recordings that include customer data are redacted; we provide timestamps and procedural logs. The evidence manifest enumerates which of these are immediate vs. multi-day.

3) Third-party BOM: We can deliver a tagged inventory CSV (example attached in the crosswalk) plus excerpts from the master SLA for our infra providers. The full SLA text is gated but we can provide redacted excerpts relevant to uptime and data handling within 72 hours.

Deliverables and schedule (confirmed):
- 2027-10-29: updated crosswalk with indicators for "Immediate (48–72h)" and "Full substantiation (by 11/04)" — delivered.
- 2027-11-02: evidence manifest updated and preliminary artifacts uploaded to the Drive intake folder (links below).
- 2027-11-05 10:00 PT: 30-minute walkthrough (calendar invite to follow).

Attachments: kms-key-rotation-summary.pdf, redwood_evidence_manifest.csv (updated)

If either of you need legal-verified attestation wording before the committee meeting, flag it and I'll loop in legal.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Applied Security — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Phone: +1 650-555-0199

If you want, I'll prep a short one-page summary for procurement that highlights the quick-deliver artifacts.
